summary.title: Precepts • Blog
summary.one_liner: A list of Urbit's technical maxims covering general design, specific design, attitude, theory, text style, and what counts as "real" software.
takeaways: Urbit's design favors data over code, CQRS, and pubsub, with subscribers never affecting publishers.
Correctness is prioritized over performance, with optimizations such as jets added on top of a correct core (e.g. Nock).
Arvo's event-log design gives constant-time event processing by keeping state in memory and checkpointing to disk.
Software is judged 'real' by determinism, decentralization, ownership, and permanence, and system modules aim to be timeless via Kelvin versioning.
Several attitude and theory maxims argue for mastering code courageously and alternating between theory and practice.
summary.summary: The page is a list of short technical maxims that the Urbit project says define its approach to engineering, grouped into sections: General Design, Specific Design, Attitude, Theory, Text Style, and Real Software. Each maxim is a one-line principle, such as "Data is better than code" or "Correctness is more important than performance," and some include brief justifications or examples. The author notes that a longer justification follows the summary list, but this page is mainly the list itself. Examples cited include Nock and jets, Arvo's event log and checkpointing, and Kelvin versioning for system modules.
